title: fix(sqlite): inspect schema metadata in one read snapshot
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow and internally inconsistent SQLite schema inspection when metadata lives on network-backed storage or changes between related reads.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway startup and schema verification inspect metadata from one committed snapshot, avoiding repeated lock acquisitions without changing schema repair behavior or requiring transaction-control authorization.

There is no schema-format, schema-version, migration, retention, or permission change. A continuous read snapshot can make rollback-journal writers wait or delay WAL checkpoint progress. Inspection and subsequent repair remain separate phases.

## Why This Change Was Made

Schema comparison and canonical-index inspection previously issued related metadata reads independently. A stepped `schema_version` statement now pins SQLite’s implicit read transaction until inspection finishes, then releases it before repair writes. This preserves top-level and nested read-only authorizers because it does not issue `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, or `SAVEPOINT`.

Review found and fixed a recovery bug: failed initial snapshot acquisition could leave a cached statement carrying `SQLITE_BUSY`, making the next inspection fail even after the writer released its lock. The first cursor step is now inside the cleanup guard.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `990531b0e1306546f4c701e9c0d0d677cf876723`.

[Full review and Crabbox A/B evidence, including all samples and the reproducible runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156108#issuecomment-5788287576).

- **Same-Testbox A/B, 50.004 MiB SQLite file:** 20 alternating A/B pairs per operation, real shared-state schema with 128 explicit indexes, synthetic payload, Linux/ext4, Node 24.19.0 / SQLite 3.53.3. Median open–inspect–close wall time: schema **41.08 → 37.93 ms** (7.7% lower); index metadata **32.00 → 28.54 ms** (10.8% lower); whole-file integrity plus index inspection **37.61 → 33.05 ms** (12.1% lower). Every result matched and the file hash stayed unchanged.
- **Important limitation:** full fresh Node/tsx source-process wall time was slower—schema harness **399.91 → 496.97 ms**, with similar overhead in the other modes. The measured inspection phase improved, but this is **not an end-to-end Gateway startup speedup claim**. Current-head NFS latency and cold OS-cache behavior were not measured; the original 7,182 → 29 ms NFS result is historical only.
- **Confirmed red/green regression:** exclusive writer lock → failed snapshot acquisition → writer rollback → immediate cached retry fails on the original PR head and passes on this head. WAL schema/index consistency, callback-error cleanup, fresh reads, and enclosing-transaction rollback are also covered.
- **164 focused Node tests passed; 20/20 passed on the repository-pinned Bun runtime.** Changed-file costs with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: snapshot suite 4 tests, **1.60 s wall**; index suite 16 tests, **1.58 s wall**.
- **63/63 existing-database/startup compatibility tests passed on the same Testbox**, including non-mutating preflight, legacy/additive schema admission, drift/refusal, cached-handle invalidation, multi-agent index repair, restart idempotency, and retained records. Test wrapper wall: **67.32 s**. No new migration is needed for this read-scope-only change.
- Changed formatting, core/test typechecks, lint, ratchets, dead-export, database-first, schema-version and architecture checks passed. Independent follow-up review validated the recovery repair without further P0–P2 working-tree findings.
- Local compatibility execution hit a subprocess-compiler `oneshot canceled` before its tests ran. The completed Testbox run supplies that proof; the local harness issue is not claimed fixed.
